headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and cascading errors; data leakage and capability conflicts are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and uses tools as nodes, while transformers reads files and can run browsers/subprocesses. A shared filesystem or copied outputs create a plausible injection bridge, but no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a writes attacker-controlled content into a shared file that agent_b later reads as instructions
IF agent_b ingests Flowise-generated text without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic file ingestion in agent_b
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent files
Require manual review before tool execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, and has broad network egress; transformers reads files and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive chatflow data can flow into model or hub requests. The profiles do not prove default sharing, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or uploaded-file store
IF either agent sends file contents to an external API during normal operation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and read, and both support multiple instances. Flowise explicitly shares state via server datastore, while transformers can spawn subprocesses and install packages. Concurrent writes to the same directory or datastore can corrupt state or overwrite artifacts; uncertainty about locking warrants high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF either agent mutates shared model, cache, or workflow files without locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is an orchestration layer whose outputs can become downstream inputs, and transformers can execute scripts or pipelines from files. If Flowise-generated text or tool outputs are treated as authoritative by transformers, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or code execution. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so high is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without validation
IF agent_a routes untrusted content into a transformer pipeline or example script
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Block shell execution on untrusted inputs
Log and diff all intermediate artifacts
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between stages

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. The only concrete compliance concern is that Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials while transformers handles files and model artifacts; without a documented mismatch, the risk is limited and not provably present.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through a deployment with stricter retention than the other agent
IF one agent logs secrets or regulated content while the other does not
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
